jobs.occupation: Clinical Professor of breast cancer therapy
jobs.description:
The Department of Clinical Medicine, Faculty of Health, Aarhus University, in collaboration with the Department of Oncology, Aarhus University Hospital, invites applications for a position as Clinical Professor of breast cancer therapy, commencing 1 September 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position is a permanent, combined appointment at Aarhus University and Aarhus University Hospital. It includes 40% of working time for research and other university duties. The department guarantees that this share can be increased to at least 50% if the successful candidate secures external funding for the remaining 10%.

As a Clinical Professor at the Department of Clinical Medicine, you will be part of what is probably the largest health science research department in Denmark. Our clinical research covers all the medical specialties and takes place in close collaboration with the university hospital and the regional hospitals in the Central Denmark Region. We have approx. 30,000 square metres of modern research facilities for experimental surgery and medicine, animal facilities and also advanced scanners at our disposal. The department has overall responsibility for the Master's degree programs in medicine and in molecular medicine. At the department we are approx. 670 academic employees, 500 PhD students and 160 technical/administrative employees who are cooperating across disciplines. As a Clinical Professor, you will be working at Aarhus University Hospital or another hospital in the Central Denmark Region. You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Your job responsibilities
As Clinical Professor of breast cancer therapy, you will have joint responsibility for the development of the department's research and teaching environment, and you will contribute to the implementation of the faculty's overall research strategy. You are expected to contribute – both independently and in collaboration with others – to the development of the department by leading research of high international quality and contributing to ensuring a high academic and didactic standard in teaching. Qua your excellent collaborative skills and a broad academic network, you contribute to the academic development at Aarhus University and to the university’s profile both nationally and internationally.

Your main tasks will consist of:

• Development pf high quality oncology research in the department
• Carry out the organization and implementation of local and national studies
• Establish national and local PhD projects
• Ensure a strong representation in relevant Danish Multidisciplinary Cancer Groups (DMCG’s) and Scientific Societies
• Contribute to maintaining and developing the department's international relations
• Research of high international quality, including publication in international journals
• Teaching, supervision and examination of Bachelor’s and Master's degree students
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination on an international level
• Contribute to the funding of your own research group with the help of external research funding
• Supervision of PhD students and contributing to assessment and committee work at Aarhus University.
• Dissemination of your research to the outside world
During your employment at Aarhus University, you will report to the Clinical Professor and Chair of Oncology.

Your competences 
You must be qualified to practice at consultant level, with documented specialist expertise and clinical experience equivalent to that of a senior hospital consultant.

You have an excellent track record on breast cancer therapy research, and you have established yourself as a prominent researcher. You possess solid research and teaching qualifications at a high international level. You have broad international cooperative partnerships and great experience of research partnerships with private and public-sector stakeholders. You have also a documented ability to attract significant competitive research funding from national and international funding bodies. You collaborate with a range of national and international breast cancer clinicians and physicists to ensure national and international accrual of patients into your clinical studies. 

As s person, you are a helpful and motivational leader who inspires other researchers and build trusting relationships with students, colleagues and partners. As a lecturer you communicate the newest and relevant knowledge in a committed, clear and comprehensible manner. As a supervisor you are competent, inspiring, supportive and responsible.

You are ready to take co-responsibility for the development of the department's research and education at the highest international level and for ensuring that we maintain a good work environment. You naturally involve yourself in interdisciplinary collaboration at departmental, faculty and university level as well as nationally and internationally.

As a Clinical Professor you are expected to inspire and raise the academic level in the clinic, and are expected to help elevate clinical tasks to a high level.

We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English. International applicants are expected to learn Danish, and Aarhus University arranges Danish teaching.

In order to be assessed as qualified for a Professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Clinical Professor and Chair of Oncology, Signe Borgquist tel.: (+45 2262 4525).

Your place of work will be the Department of Oncology, Palle Juul-Jensen Boulevard 99, 8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Terms of employment
• In making the appointment, emphasis will be placed on a high degree of original production at an internal level and experience from teaching at different levels as well as contributions to the development of teaching activities and teaching material, hereby documenting that the applicant has developed the academic discipline from a research and teaching perspective.
• Moreover, there will be an assessment of the applicant’s ability to perform research and teaching management tasks.
• Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
• The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (Akademikerne).
• Remuneration is in accordance with the above, and the Salary agreement catalogue for staff at Health.
• Further information on qualification requirements and job description can be found in the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

Application
Your application must include the following:

• Motivated application
• Curriculum Vitae
• Diploma
• Template for applicant - professor
• A list of publications
• A teaching portfolio. We refer to Guideline on the use of teaching portfolios
• The ten publications stated as the most important in the 'Template for applicant - professor' must be submitted
• Research plan, which is part of the 'Template to applicant - professor' can be uploaded separately (optional)
• Coauthor statement(s) can be uploaded (optional)
• References/recommendations can be uploaded separately in the e-recruitment system (optional)
We refer to the faculty’s Guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

 

International applicant?
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.occupation: Removing micropollutants and oxidation products by biofilm reactors (Project Optimise)
jobs.description:
The project will focus on developing and testing innovative bioreactors for ozonation post treatment (especially for removal of ozonation products) for wastewater treatment. The system will be developed in labscale but its relevance will be tested by analysing ozonation products and organic micro pollutants in a small catchment receiving ozonated wastewater. Some samples will be analysed by partners by means of biosensing. Some sampling for micropollutants and ozonation products in recipients is part of optimize.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a 22 months position from 1st April 2027 or as soon possible.

Job description

•   Develop biofilm reactors for ozonation post treatment of wastewater

•   Analysing ozonation products and organic micro pollutants in wastewater

•   Analysing ozonation products and organic micro pollutants in recipient

•   Documentation, reporting and publishing

Applicants must hold a PhD in environmental engineering, environmental chemistry, environmental science or similar.

Experiences in i)biofilm engineering and ii)biofilm reactors, iii)quantitation of organic micropollutants by means of HPLC-MS/MS and/or HPLC-HR-MS/MS, iv)publishing results, v)collaboration in a multinational environment and vi) reporting are helpful, as well as vii)interactions with wastewater treatment plants. Some of these can be developed during the project.

Who we are

Most scientific information on the group is available under  https://projects.au.dk/waterpurification//

The group has own ozonation and biofilm reactors as well as two triple quad HPLC-MS/MS systems, two HPLC-MS/MS systems with high resolution and one imaging mass spectrometer.

Place of work and area of employment

Aarhus University, Department of Environmental Science, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde

Contact information

Interested candidates are welcome to contact: Prof. Kai Bester (kb@envs.au.dk or +4593508089)

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than January 4, 2027.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Take full responsibility for warehouse operations, inventory management and stock accuracy in an international project organisation.

Copenhagen Global A/S is part of Copenhagen Group, a Danish project-driven organisation with a strong international profile. We tender for and manage complex projects for international organisations and national authorities, operating across different markets and in close cooperation with specialised partners.

Our activities place high demands on structured warehouse operations, accurate inventory management and reliable stock control. To support this, we are looking for an experienced and detail-oriented Warehouse & Inventory Controller to take full responsibility for Copenhagen Global's warehouse, working closely with colleagues to ensure that all goods, equipment and materials are properly registered, stored and managed.

Your Responsibilities

You will have overall responsibility for the day-to-day operations of Copenhagen Global's warehouse, ensuring accurate stock records and effective inventory control.

Your responsibilities will include registering incoming and outgoing goods, maintaining accurate inventory records and ensuring that all materials and equipment are correctly identified, stored and accounted for. You will be responsible for maintaining and updating the warehouse management system, ensuring that physical stock levels match recorded inventory.

You will also plan and conduct regular stocktakes, identify and resolve discrepancies, and maintain clear procedures for stock handling, storage and inventory control, ensuring that all inventory records are continuously updated and accurately maintained in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

In addition, you will coordinate the receipt and dispatch of goods, support logistical requirements across Copenhagen Global's projects and work closely with colleagues in procurement, project management and other relevant functions.

You will take ownership of maintaining a well-organised, safe and efficient warehouse, ensuring that materials and equipment are accessible, traceable and handled in accordance with established procedures.

The role requires a high degree of independence, accountability and attention to detail.

Your Background

We are looking for someone with previous experience in warehouse management, including direct responsibility for inventory control and goods registration.

You have practical experience with warehouse management or inventory systems and understand the importance of accurate registration, stock reconciliation and traceability. You are confident working with digital systems and maintaining structured, reliable inventory records.

You are highly detail-oriented, systematic and reliable, with a strong sense of responsibility and the ability to maintain an overview of a wide range of materials, equipment and ongoing activities.

You are proactive in identifying discrepancies and improving procedures, and you take pride in maintaining an organised warehouse where stock levels and the location of goods can be accounted for at all times.

You are comfortable working independently, prioritising tasks and coordinating with colleagues across different functions. You communicate effectively in Danish and English.

Relevant experience in logistics or project-driven warehouse operations, preferably involving the use of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, will be considered an advantage.

Practical Information

The position is based at our warehouse facilities in Copenhagen.

Salary will reflect qualifications and experience.

Employment is conditional upon obtaining the required security clearance.

Join Vattenfall as an Asset Integrity Engineer and take a leading technical role in safeguarding the long-term integrity, reliability and performance of Hollandse Kust Zuid (HKZ). You will translate asset condition, operational experience and technical risk into clear priorities and practical interventions, helping the organisation make well-founded decisions across maintenance, inspections, technical improvements and long-term asset planning.

Step into a vital role where your expertise in Asset Integrity Management ensures that our offshore wind farms operate reliably, safely, and sustainably. As an Asset Integrity Engineer within the Integrated Operations team at Vattenfall, you will help optimize the operational life and yield of our wind farms, with a clear operational interface to our offshore activities.

You will work with diverse stakeholders across Offshore Engineering, Asset Management, and Operations to strengthen our Asset Integrity Management framework, ensuring a continued focus on optimizing the operational life and yield of HKZ as well as contributing to our broader portfolio of operating assets.

Join us and power the journey toward a fossil-free future by shaping how we manage the integrity of complex, large-scale renewable energy assets. You will be part of a growing team within Business Area (BA) Wind, with a special focus on Offshore Generation—the organization fully accountable for operating and maintaining our offshore wind farms in a healthy, safe, and cost-efficient manner.

Your role / what will you do? As our new Asset Integrity Engineer in Asset Integrity, you will collaborate with various stakeholders in Technical Integrity Management to develop and maintain a robust framework for managing risk, condition monitoring, and maintenance activities for offshore wind assets.

You will act as a key focal point for integrity issues at HKZ, working closely with internal Technical Authorities to identify and mitigate risks related to WTG, cables, foundations, offshore structures, substations, and more.

You will help shape how Vattenfall leverages data and analytics to support Asset Integrity, ensuring that our condition monitoring, inspection, and maintenance programs drive continuous improvement. You will also engage in root cause analyses, contribute to project delivery and operational optimization programs, and lead change management initiatives to optimize asset performance over the long term.

The role supports asset integrity activities with a particular focus on HKZ, while contributing to Asset Integrity activities and knowledge sharing across our wider operating fleet as required.

Key Responsibilities:

As part of Integrated Operation and fully deployed to support our Asset Integrity Team:

• Being part of the continuous development of the Asset Integrity Management framework, delivering a systematic approach to Asset Integrity Management.

• Report accurately on the performance, status and health of HKZ and support consistent Asset Integrity reporting across our operating fleet.

• Ensure the integrity of HKZ is understood and appropriately managed, while supporting readiness within Asset Integrity for our future projects.

• Proactively support Integrity issues at HKZ and, where relevant, across our operating fleet and asset projects.

• In Collaboration with the different disciplines across Generation & Engineering ensure data availability to support Risk Based & Condition based maintenance Programs.

• Outline and support all condition monitoring, inspection and maintenance data collection activities, collate and integrate data to AIM-D and CMMS systems, so it supports the Asset Integrity Framework and quality in our Asset integrity reporting.

• Work with change management and root cause analysis to support HKZ, the operating fleet and projects.

• Work with our technical authorities/specialists to develop appropriate and cost-effective risk mitigation strategies and review external repair recommendations.

• Engage in assignments in product development, Classification of consequence, project delivery or operational assets as required for asset integrity management at HKZ and for future sites.

• Prepare and update key technology and process documents within Asset Integrity Management.

• Work with project management on operational optimisation programs.

Location

Kolding, Amsterdam, London or Hamburg.

Qualifications

Your profile / who are you?

As our Asset Integrity Engineer, you will bring an understanding of Asset Integrity Management across large-scale industrial or offshore environments. You excel at translating technical insights into practical maintenance strategies, thrive on interdisciplinary teamwork, and remain forward-thinking in a fast-evolving renewable energy landscape. Your ability to spot critical risks early, manage data effectively, and communicate clearly will be key to driving continuous improvement at HKZ and across our offshore wind portfolio.

Next to this, you bring:

• Preferably five years experience managing integrity for large-scale energy assets, ensuring proactive risk mitigation.

• Demonstrated proficiency in root cause analysis with a results-oriented, systematic approach.

• Knowledge of data analytics tools (e.g., Python, CMMS) and experience interpreting condition monitoring insights would be an advantage, but is not essential.

• Experience setting up risk-based and condition-based maintenance programs aligned with operational goals.

• Strong stakeholder management skills, collaborating seamlessly with Technical Authorities, Operations, and Engineering.

• Excellent communication in English, conveying complex technical issues to diverse audiences.

• A proactive, solution-focused mindset, consistently seeking innovative ways to meet our fossil-free mission.

Additional Information

Our offer

Good remuneration, a challenging and international work environment, and the possibility to work with some of the best in the field. You will be working in interdisciplinary teams and you can always count on support from committed colleagues. We offer attractive employment conditions and opportunities for personal and professional development.

More Information

We welcome your application in English, no later than, December 3rd 2026. We kindly request that you do not send applications by any means other than via our website and that you refrain from submitting a cover letter with your application. You apply quickly and easily by answering screening questions and attaching your CV.

For more information about the recruitment process you are welcome to contact our recruiter Anne Vriesema via anne.vriesema@vattenfall.com

Our team consists of around 70 people from diverse backgrounds and nationalities, brought together by a shared belief in team effort, community, and delivering quality products and solutions.

We are currently using Node.js (mainly TypeScript), Kubernetes, MySQL, and BigQuery on the backend, hosted on Google Cloud Platform. Having scaled our backend to a global presence, we rely heavily on Infrastructure as Code using Terraform. We believe in releasing early and often, supported by an automated CI/CD pipeline running multiple daily deployments.

Our engineers work in agile, cross-functional teams of 3–4 people with minimal overhead and bureaucracy. We empower our teams with full decision-making power over how they work, what they focus on, and how they deliver functionality.

jobs.occupation: Head of Translational Medicine and Early Development
jobs.description:
Turn scientific promise into clinical progress. Build the proof-of-concept engine that helps LEO Pharma make smarter development decisions and bring meaningful innovation closer to patients.

Shape What Comes Next

How would you connect emerging biology, quantitative insights, and clinical expertise to shape the next generation of development programs? At LEO Pharma, you will lead Translational Medicine & Early Development, bringing together people, partners, and evidence to answer critical questions early. This is an opportunity to build capabilities, influence portfolio decisions, and connect scientific ambition with a clear path to clinical proof of concept.

Your role

You will build and lead an integrated proof-of-concept engine, translating biological hypotheses into clinically testable, quantitatively informed, decision-ready programs. Working across internal teams and external partners, you will establish mechanism-based rationales, meaningful patient strategies, and robust development plans. Your focus will be on generating the evidence needed to select doses, assess benefit–risk, and guide progression toward registrational studies.

Your primary responsibilities will be to:

• Lead translational and early-development strategy across programs, developing people leaders and subject-matter experts.

• Partner with Science, Search & Innovation and clinical teams to design early-phase studies demonstrating target engagement, proof of mechanism, and patient relevance.

• Integrate biomarkers, patient stratification, quantitative pharmacology, and modelling and simulation to optimize doses, regimens, endpoints, and study designs.

• Support clinical due diligence and integration of externally sourced assets, building partnerships that strengthen translational capabilities.

• Shape regulatory and cross-functional evidence strategies, translating complex findings into clear recommendations for project teams and governance forums.

You will also establish progression criteria and performance indicators that strengthen decision quality, evidence maturity, execution, and resource efficiency. Throughout early development, you will ensure efficacy hypotheses are considered alongside safety, tolerability, and therapeutic index.

Your Qualifications

You bring scientific depth and leadership experience, with the ability to connect translational evidence to clinical and portfolio decisions.

We are looking for:

• An advanced degree in Medicine, Pharmacology, Translational Science, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related discipline; MD and PhD qualifications are preferred.

• Significant leadership experience in translational medicine, clinical pharmacology, and/or early clinical development within biotech or pharma.

• Demonstrated expertise in early-phase studies in patients and healthy participants, linking mechanisms of action and biomarkers to dose selection and development strategy.

• A track record of building high-performing global teams, developing people, and integrating external assets and partnerships.

• Experience contributing to regulatory submissions and evidence generation supporting registration and market access.

Experience with externally sourced innovation is strongly preferred; dermatology and/or rare-disease experience is beneficial. You combine strategic thinking with curiosity, sound judgment, and a collaborative approach, influencing effectively across a matrix organization.

Your new team

You will lead Translational Medicine & Early Development, with two line managers as direct reports, the group is in total 20 employees. You will report to the Vice President, Head of Global Clinical Development.

Your network will span clinical development, skin science, regulatory, safety, market access, and commercial colleagues. Together with external collaborators, you will connect expertise across disciplines to strengthen early development.

Contact and application

For additional information, please contact Talent Acquisition Partner, Sabina Ravn Lebech at saleb@leo-pharma.com

You do not need to upload a cover letter, but feel free to add a few sentences in your resume or CV on why this position has your interest.

Beyond the skin

jobs.occupation: Har du lyst til at arbejde som pædagogisk vikar i et dagtilbud, hvor mange vælger at blive lidt længere?
jobs.description:
Måske overvejer du at arbejde med børn i 0-6-årsområdet og vil gerne prøve det af først. Måske er du studerende, holder sabbatår – eller har brug for et fleksibelt job, hvor du selv kan byde ind på vagter, når det passer dig.

I Børnehuset Nørreskoven søger vi pædagogiske vikarer, som har lyst til at være en del af hverdagen, når der er brug for ekstra hænder – og som trives i et børnehus med nærhed, varme og tydelige rammer. 
Som vikar hos os

bliver du taget godt imod. Du skal ikke kunne det hele på forhånd – det vigtigste er, at du har lyst til at være sammen med børnene og indgå i hverdagen på stuerne.

Dine opgaver kan blandt andet være:

• at indgå i hverdagen på vuggestue- eller børnehavestuer
• at lege, læse, være med i rutiner og på legepladsen
• at træde til dér, hvor der er brug for dig
• at bidrage til en tryg og god dag for børnene
Har du særlig interesse i at hjælpe til i køkkenet sammen med en erfaren medarbejder, er det en ekstra fordel. Skriv det endelig i din ansøgning.

Vi gør os umage for, at det skal være overskueligt og trygt at være vikar – også hvis du er ny i dagtilbud.
Hvem kan søge?

Vi forventer, at du:

• har lyst til at arbejde i et dagtilbud og være sammen med børn
• er fleksibel, mødestabil og god til at overholde aftaler
• møder børn og kolleger med godt humør
• ikke er bange for at tage fat og spørge, hvis du er i tvivl
• er nysgerrig og har lyst til at lære
• ikke er bange for at give en hånd med i hele huset
• At du kan starte hurtigst mulligt

 
Det er en klar fordel, hvis du har erfaring med børn eller dagtilbud – men det er ikke et krav. Vi tager imod både erfarne og uddannede profiler og dig, der gerne vil afprøve området og finde ud af, om arbejdet med børn er noget for dig. Vi har tidligere haft gode erfaringer med, at vikarer udvikler sig og senere går videre i uddannelse eller fast job – også hos os.
Derfor trives mange vikarer hos os

Vi oplever, at mange af vores vikarer er glade for at være i Nørreskoven og ofte vælger at blive hængende, mens de finder ud af, hvad næste skridt for dem skal være. Det ser vi som et tegn på, at hverdagen er rar at være i, og at man føler sig velkommen og taget alvorligt.

Hos os får du:

• et lille børnehus med masser af charme – hvor alle kender alle
• imødekommende og hjælpsomme kolleger i alle aldre
• en arbejdsdag med smil, grin og liv
• virkelig søde og engagerede forældre
• mulighed for at arbejde i både vuggestue og børnehave

Vi har 2 vuggestuegrupper med 12 børn på hver og 3 børnehavegrupper med ca. 20 børn i hver. Der er masser af muligheder for at lege, læse, cykle, spille bold, lave bål og være ude – alt sammen med fokus på at skabe det bedste børneliv.

Har du lyst til at prøve kræfter i køkkenet, har vi også et moderne køkken og en køkkendame, der gerne tager dig med.
Lidt om Børnehuset Nørreskoven

Vi er en integreret institution med vuggestue og børnehave. Huset er omgivet af en stor legeplads med mange legemuligheder, et lille “bjerg” og et bålhus. Når du træder ind i huset, møder du et sted, der oser af charme, nærhed og hverdagsliv – og hvor der er plads til nye ansigter.
Det praktiske

Børnehuset Nørreskoven ligger meget centralt i Værløse, tæt på bymidten og med særdeles nem adgang med tog, bus, cykel og bil. Det gør det let at komme til og fra – også når vagterne ligger forskelligt.

Stillingen er som vikar med varierende antal timer. Du er velkommen til at fortælle os om dine ønsker, og vi vil så vidt muligt forsøge at imødekomme dem.

Praktisk

Der indhentes referencer fra tidligere ansættelsesforhold, hvis du kommer i betragtning til stillingen.

I Furesø Kommune sker løn og ansættelsesvilkår efter gældende overenskomst og ud fra principperne i Ny Løn.

Vi gør opmærksom på, at din private e-mail og/ eller telefonnummer bliver videregivet til faglig organisation i forbindelse med forhandling af løn.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Experimental Parasitology at Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a 1 year and 6 months position to commence 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

The postdoc will be part of the Parasites, Immunology and Gut Health (PIGH) group in the Section for Parasitology and Pathology.

A list of the group’s publications can be found at:

https://scholar.google.dk/citations?hl=en&user=70v-4RoAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate

Information on the department can be found at: https://ivh.ku.dk 

Our group and research
The PIGH group is interested in how dietary components and the gut microbiota interact to regulate type-2 immunity at mucosal surfaces, which is critical for protection against helminth parasites but can also cause pathologies such as allergies when dysregulated. We apply small (rodent) and large (swine) animal models and in vitro cell culture techniques to explore host-pathogen-microbiome interactions and nutritional immunology. The group is a multidisciplinary team embedded within the Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, with close links to other sections working on diseases, food chemistry, natural product chemistry, and the gut microbiome. Our aims are to develop novel therapies to prevent infection and disease in animals and humans. The group is international in nature, and the daily working language is English.

Your job 

In this position, you will work on a project exploring interactions between helminths and the host gut microbiome. We are particularly interested in how diet-driven changes in the host gut microbiome impact the parasite infectivity and host resistance. The main role of the postdoc will be to carry out research involving dietary manipulations and experimental parasite infections in laboratory animals. This will be coupled with extensive microbiome analyses including both amplicon-based sequencing approaches and shotgun (metagenomic) approaches and associated bioinformatic analyses. Furthermore, the duties of the Postdoc will include supporting the overall research goals of the group and contributing to a positive and supportive group environment that emphasizes teamwork, curiosity and positivity.

The postdoc’s responsibilities will primarily consist of: 

• 
research, including publication/academic dissemination duties

• 
research-based teaching

• 
sharing knowledge with society

 Furthermore, we are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following skills and experience:

Essential experience and skills:

• 
You have a PhD in parasitology, biology or related field

• 
You are experienced in laboratory animal models, including experimental parasite infections, with FELASA accreditation or equivalent.

• 
You have experience in gut microbiome analytical techniques

• 
Demonstrated record of peer-reviewed publications.

• 
Proficient communication skills and ability to work in teams.

• 
Excellent English skills written and spoken.

 Desirable experience and skills:

• 
Experience with transcriptomics and immunology techniques (e.g. flow cytometry).

• 
You have an active interest in nutrition and/or gut health.

Place of employment

The place of employment is at the Section for Parasitology and Pathology, Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and animal facilities.

Terms of employment 

The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 1 year and 6 months. The start date is 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW

Questions
For further information please contact Professor Andrew Williams arw@sund.ku.dk 

Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

Application procedure
Your application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

• 
Motivated letter of application (Max. one page)

• 
CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

• 
A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do

• 
List of publications

Deadline for applications: 6 December 2026, 23.59pm CET 

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

The further process 
After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

Interviews are expected to be held in week 2, 2027

The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Electrical Engineering: Novel NMR Instrumentation for Groundwater Measurements
jobs.description:
Do you want to help develop novel instrumentation for groundwater investigations? At the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aarhus University, we are seeking a motivated postdoctoral researcher in electrical engineering to contribute to the development of novel nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) instruments for groundwater characterization. You will join an interdisciplinary research environment spanning electrical engineering, geophysics, and environmental science working on technologies that can improve our understanding of vital groundwater resources. The 2-year position is based in Aarhus, Denmark and is available from 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a 2–year position from 1 March 2027 or as soon possible thereafter.

Job description

We are seeking a postdoctoral researcher in electrical engineering to help develop a new generation of surface NMR instruments for groundwater characterization. Through a recently funded research project, we are building a new instrument with capabilities beyond those of existing systems. As part of the project, you will play a central role in designing and integrating key electronic subsystems and in exploring how the resulting instrument can open new possibilities for groundwater investigations.

Your tasks will include

• Design, simulation, construction, and validation of electronic subsystems

• Interfacing of ADCs and DACs to analog frontends and a microcontroller

• Integration of subsystems into a complete instrument

• Experimental work, including testing of instruments and data collection in both laboratory and field environments

• Data analysis

• Co-supervision of bachelor and master thesis projects within the project

• Documentation of technical development and research results

• Leading and contributing to scientific publications

You will join a collaborative and interdisciplinary team where you will be working closely with other researchers, technicians, and students at the Department. The project also involves interaction with researchers and end-users working directly with groundwater characterization.

Your profile

Applicants should hold a PhD in electrical engineering or similar.

Prior experience with surface NMR or groundwater measurements is not required, but we expect you to a have a curiosity for these areas.

We are looking for candidates with experience in several of the following areas:

• Electronic systems design

• Development of low-noise analog and digital electronics including power supplies

• Interfacing to/from ADCs and DACs

• PCB layout

• Solving EMC issues

• Practical electronic and laboratory skills

• Data analysis

Experience in one or more of the following areas is considered advantageous:

• Real-time data acquisition systems implemented on microcontrollers

• Embedded Linux

• Power electronics

• Signal processing and embedded signal processing

It is also advantageous if you have a driver’s license.

Personal skills

You have good English skills, both in speaking and in writing. You take responsibility for assigned tasks and communicate openly about progress, challenges, and ideas. You can work independently as well as in a team. You are open-minded, curious, and have a good sense of humour. We value the ability to work independently as well as in a team.

We encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences. If you believe you are a strong match for the position but do not meet every listed qualification, we would still like to hear from you.

Who we are

The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at Aarhus University is a leading research institution committed to excellence in research, education, and innovation. The department hosts research spanning electronics, signal processing, embedded systems, sensing technologies, artificial intelligence, biomedical engineering, digital twins, power electronics, and many other areas, creating opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and knowledge exchange.

This position will be supervised by Associate Professor Jakob Juul Larsen, whose current research focuses on surface NMR instrumentation, methodology, and applications.

What we offer

We offer a vibrant and inclusive research environment with a clear commitment to real-world impact. This position provides a rare opportunity to help shape the development of an entirely new scientific instrument, from subsystem design and implementation to system integration, testing, and scientific application. You will have substantial technical responsibility and the opportunity to influence both the engineering solutions and the future research capabilities of the instrument. Denmark is consistently ranked among the best countries in the world for work-life balance and quality of life. Family-friendly policies include generous parental leave, subsidised childcare, and access to excellent public healthcare and education. As a postdoc at Aarhus University, you will benefit from a supportive and flexible workplace culture that values diversity and offers excellent conditions for researchers and their families.

Specifically, we offer:

• A central role in the development of a new surface NMR instrument with unique capabilities for groundwater characterization;

• Opportunities to work across the full development chain, from electronics design and system integration to field deployment and scientific application;

• Access to state-of-the-art laboratory facilities and research infrastructure;

• Strong support for research career development, including mentoring and international networking opportunities;

• A workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is Finlandsgade 22, 8200 Aarhus N, Denmark, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information

For further information, please contact: Associate Professor Jakob Juul Larsen, + 45 4189 3273, jjl@ece.au.dk_._

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than 4 January 2027.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.
